items.title: Constitutional posts & key appointments (2025-26)
items.body:
**In one line.** Who holds India's top constitutional and institutional offices in 2026.

**Why it is asked.** Current office-holders are the single most predictable current-affairs questions, and the exam swaps one incumbent for a predecessor to trap you.

| Post | Incumbent | Since |
|---|---|---|
| President | Droupadi Murmu | 25 Jul 2022 |
| Vice-President | C. P. Radhakrishnan | 12 Sep 2025 |
| Prime Minister | Narendra Modi | 26 May 2014 |
| Chief Justice of India, CJI (53rd) | Surya Kant | 24 Nov 2025 |
| Lok Sabha Speaker | Om Birla | 19 Jun 2019 |
| Chief Election Commissioner, CEC | Gyanesh Kumar | 19 Feb 2025 |
| RBI Governor (26th) | Sanjay Malhotra | 11 Dec 2024 |

**Points to note**

- **C. P. Radhakrishnan** became the 15th Vice-President after **Jagdeep Dhankhar** resigned. The Vice-President is, by virtue of the office, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Article 64 (he presides over the upper house).
- **Surya Kant** is the 53rd **CJI** (Chief Justice of India); the recent order was Chandrachud (50th), Sanjiv Khanna (51st), B. R. Gavai (52nd), Surya Kant (53rd).
- **Gyanesh Kumar** is the **CEC** (Chief Election Commissioner) chosen under the new selection framework of the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023.

**Don't confuse.** The CJI changed (Gavai → Surya Kant) but the President, Vice-President and PM did not — options often slip in an outdated CJI name.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- President = Droupadi Murmu (since 25 Jul 2022, 15th President).
- Vice-President = C. P. Radhakrishnan (since 12 Sep 2025), ex-officio Rajya Sabha Chairman.
- Surya Kant is the 53rd CJI, sworn in 24 Nov 2025, succeeding B. R. Gavai.
- Gyanesh Kumar is Chief Election Commissioner since 19 Feb 2025.
- Sanjay Malhotra is the 26th RBI Governor since 11 Dec 2024 (after Shaktikanta Das).

items.title: Economic Survey 2025-26 & Union Budget 2026-27
items.body:
**In one line.** What the 2025-26 Economic Survey projected and the main features of the 2026-27 Union Budget.

**Why it is asked.** The growth number, the Survey theme, and the Budget date/presenter are standard questions; the new Income Tax Act is a fresh high-yield fact.

**Economic Survey 2025-26.** The Survey is a yearly economic report placed in Parliament by the **Finance Minister** just before the Budget. It is prepared by the Economic Division of the **DEA** (Department of Economic Affairs) under the **Chief Economic Adviser (CEA)**, the government's top economist.
- **Real GDP growth for FY26: 7.4%**; **GVA** (Gross Value Added — output measured at producer prices) growth 7.3%; **FY27 outlook 6.8-7.2%** — keeping India the fastest-growing major economy.
- Theme: India moving from **'Strategic Resilience' to 'Strategic Indispensability'**.
- Private Final Consumption was about 61.5% of GDP (highest since 2012); **GFCF** (Gross Fixed Capital Formation — investment in fixed assets) rose 7.8%.
- The Survey was first **merged with the Budget in 1950-51** and became a **separate document in 1964**.

**Union Budget 2026-27.** Presented by Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2026** (the Budget is the Annual Financial Statement required by Article 112). The new **Income Tax Act, 2025** replaced the six-decade-old Income-tax Act, 1961, with effect from **1 April 2026**.

**Don't confuse.** The Economic Survey became a *separate* document in 1964, not when it first appeared (1950-51).

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- Economic Survey 2025-26: real GDP growth FY26 = 7.4%, FY27 outlook 6.8-7.2%.
- Survey theme: 'Strategic Resilience' to 'Strategic Indispensability'; prepared under the CEA.
- Economic Survey became a separate document (from the Budget) in 1964.
- Union Budget 2026-27 presented by Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 Feb 2026.
- Income Tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act, effective 1 April 2026.

items.title: Key schemes, bills & laws (2025-26)
items.body:
**In one line.** Three centrepiece 2025-26 proposals: a new rural-jobs law, higher tobacco excise, and a new dental regulator.

**Why it is asked.** 'Which law replaces which' is a classic pairing question, and the number of guaranteed workdays is a favourite single fact.

**VBG-RAMG Bill (to replace MGNREGA).** Its full name is the **Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)**. (**MGNREGA** = Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, the law that guarantees paid rural work.) The Bill proposes to replace MGNREGA and raise the wage-work guarantee from **100 to 125 days** a year. It would require wages to be paid within **7 to 15 days**, with compensation for delay, and focus on building durable rural assets.

**Central Excise (Amendment) Bill, 2025.** It raised the **excise duty on tobacco products** — both to earn revenue and to discourage tobacco use. (Excise duty is a tax on goods made within the country; after GST, central excise mainly applies to items left outside GST such as tobacco and petroleum.)

**National Dental Commission (March 2026).** It replaced the **Dental Council of India** (created under the Dentists Act, 1948) to modernise dental education and regulation — mirroring the earlier reform when the National Medical Commission replaced the Medical Council of India in 2020.

**Remember it:** VBG-RAMG = 125 days (up from MGNREGA's 100); National Dental Commission replaced the Dental Council of India.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- VB-G RAM G = Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin); replaces MGNREGA.
- VB-G RAM G raises the employment guarantee to 125 days (from MGNREGA's 100).
- Central Excise (Amendment) Bill 2025 raised duties on tobacco products.
- National Dental Commission (Mar 2026) replaced the Dental Council of India.

items.title: Padma Awards 2026 & civilian honours
items.body:
**In one line.** The 2026 Padma awardees and where the Padma honours sit among India's civilian awards.

**Why it is asked.** The yearly Padma totals, a few marquee names, and the order of precedence are repeat questions; the 'Bhupen Hazarika awards' is a known trap.

**Padma Awards 2026.**
- **131 awards** approved: **5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan, 113 Padma Shri**; of these 19 are women, 16 posthumous, and 6 are foreigners/NRI/PIO/OCI (Non-Resident Indians / Persons of Indian Origin / Overseas Citizens of India).
- **Padma Vibhushan (5):** Dharmendra Deol (Art, posthumous), K. T. Thomas (Public Affairs), N. Rajam (Art — violinist), P. Narayanan (Literature and Education), V. S. Achuthanandan (Public Affairs, posthumous — former Kerala Chief Minister).
- **Padma Bhushan (notable):** Alka Yagnik, Mammootty, Uday Kotak, Vijay Amritraj, Bhagat Singh Koshyari; Piyush Pandey and Shibu Soren (posthumous).

**Order of civilian honours**
- **Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri** (highest to lowest).
- No new **Bharat Ratna** was conferred during November 2025 to October 2026.

**Don't confuse.** The 'Bharat Ratna Dr. Bhupen Hazarika National Awards' (November 2025, Guwahati) are separate cultural awards *named after* Hazarika — they are not the Bharat Ratna itself.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- Padma Awards 2026 total = 131 (5 Vibhushan, 13 Bhushan, 113 Shri).
- 2026 Padma Vibhushan: Dharmendra, K.T. Thomas, N. Rajam, P. Narayanan, V.S. Achuthanandan.
- Uday Kotak, Alka Yagnik, Mammootty, Vijay Amritraj received the Padma Bhushan 2026.
- Civilian honours order: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri.
- No new Bharat Ratna was announced in the Nov 2025-Oct 2026 window.

items.title: Reports & indices — India's ranks (2025-26)
items.body:
**In one line.** India's ranks across the major 2025-26 global indices.

**Why it is asked.** Index ranks and their publishers are heavily tested, and the exam deliberately swaps the index with the wrong publisher or rank.

| Index / Report | Publisher | India's rank |
|---|---|---|
| Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2026 | Germanwatch and partners | 23rd (from 10th) |
| Henley Passport Index 2026 | Henley & Partners | 80th (about 55 destinations) |
| Asia Power Index 2025 | Lowy Institute | 3rd ('major power') |
| Global AI Vibrancy Index 2025 | Stanford HAI | 3rd (score 21.59) |
| Milk production | — | 1st (about 247.87 million tonnes) |
| Creative-services exports | UNCTAD | 4th (about $94.2 billion) |

**Points to note**
- The **CCPI** (Climate Change Performance Index) always leaves its **top 3 ranks vacant**, because no country is judged fully Paris-aligned — so a '1st' CCPI answer is wrong by design.
- **Asia Power Index** order: United States (1st) > China (2nd) > **India (3rd)** > Japan (4th).
- In the **AI Vibrancy Index**, India trails only the United States and China.

**Don't confuse.** India is **1st in milk production** but only **3rd/4th** in most other indices here — do not generalise one rank to the others.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- CCPI 2026: India 23rd (slipped from 10th); top 3 ranks always left vacant.
- Henley Passport Index 2026: India 80th.
- Asia Power Index 2025 (Lowy): India 3rd, upgraded to a 'major power'.
- Global AI Vibrancy Index 2025: India 3rd, behind USA and China.
- India is No.1 in milk production (~247.87 MT) and 4th in creative-services exports.

items.title: Defence & space milestones (2025-26)
items.body:
**In one line.** India's main navy commissionings, missile tests and space milestones in 2025-26.

**Why it is asked.** 'Which ship/missile/satellite does what' is quick-recall, and the three navy items (INS Mahe, INS Aridaman) plus NISAR are easy to confuse.

**Navy commissionings.**
- **INS Mahe** — the lead ship of the **Mahe-class ASW-SWC** (Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft), built to hunt submarines close to the coast.
- **INS Aridaman** — India's **third home-built SSBN** (a nuclear-powered submarine carrying ballistic missiles), after Arihant and Arighaat, under the ATV (Advanced Technology Vessel) programme; it strengthens the sea leg of the nuclear triad (the ability to launch nuclear weapons from land, air and sea).

**Missiles and space.**
- **DRDO's LRLACM** — the Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile — was flight-tested from **Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha**; it is a subsonic, precision deep-strike missile that can be launched from the ground or a ship. (DRDO = Defence Research and Development Organisation.)
- **ISRO** (Indian Space Research Organisation): the **first PSLV built by Indian industry** (under ISRO supervision) targeted an early-2026 launch — a step towards privatised launch vehicles.
- **NISAR** — the joint **NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar** Earth-observation satellite; **Gaganyaan** (India's first crewed mission) remains ISRO's flagship goal.

**Don't confuse.** **INS Mahe** is a small coastal sub-hunter; **INS Aridaman** is a large nuclear-missile submarine — very different roles.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- INS Mahe = lead ship of the Mahe-class ASW shallow water craft.
- INS Aridaman = India's third indigenous SSBN (nuclear ballistic-missile submarine).
- DRDO's LRLACM is a Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile, tested from Abdul Kalam Island.
- First industry-built PSLV (under ISRO) targeted an early-2026 launch.
- NISAR is a joint NASA-ISRO earth-observation (SAR) satellite.

items.title: Summits, trade, sports, infrastructure & elections (2026)
items.body:
**In one line.** The 2026 summits India hosted, its new trade deals, major sporting events and the state elections.

**Why it is asked.** Host cities, FTA partners and election states are frequent single-fact questions.

**Summits and trade.**
- The **AI Impact Summit** was hosted in **New Delhi (February 2026)**, positioning India as a hub for inclusive, development-focused artificial intelligence.
- The **India-EU FTA** (Free Trade Agreement — a deal to cut tariffs between countries) was politically concluded in early 2026; the **New Zealand-India FTA** was signed in New Delhi (April 2026).

**Sports.**
- The **2026 Men's T20 World Cup** (cricket) was co-hosted by **India and Sri Lanka** (February-March 2026).
- India won hosting rights for the **2028 World Athletics Indoor Championships** (Bhubaneswar) — the 4th Asian nation to host it.

**Infrastructure and elections.**
- **Noida International Airport (Jewar, Uttar Pradesh)** was inaugurated by PM Modi on **28 March 2026**.
- **Assembly elections (April-May 2026)** were held in Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry; before them the Election Commission ran a **Special Intensive Revision (SIR)** — a thorough re-check of the voter rolls — whose validity the Supreme Court examined.

**Remember it:** AI Impact Summit = New Delhi (Feb 2026); Noida (Jewar) airport opened 28 March 2026.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- India hosted the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi (Feb 2026).
- India-EU FTA concluded and NZ-India FTA signed in New Delhi in 2026.
- 2026 Men's T20 World Cup co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka.
- Noida International Airport (Jewar, UP) inaugurated on 28 Mar 2026.
- 2026 Assembly polls: Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Puducherry; ECI ran a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of rolls.

items.title: Exam-Precision: Labour Codes, MSME, Piprahwa, NTDs, CETA & BRICS 2026
items.body:
**In one line.** Six precision facts examiners test exactly: labour codes, MSME limits, the Piprahwa relics, NTD elimination, CETA and the BRICS chair.

**Why it is asked.** These are the kinds of pin-point facts (exact dates, scripts, counts) that decide a one-mark question, so the precise detail matters more than the theme.

**Laws and economy.**
- The **four labour codes** (on Wages; Industrial Relations; Social Security; and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions) came into force **nationally on 21 November 2025**, consolidating 29 central labour laws into four.
- The **MSME** (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises) revised classification, with higher investment and turnover limits, took effect **1 April 2025** (announced in Budget 2025-26).

**Heritage and health.**
- The **Piprahwa relics** (linked to the Buddha) were first discovered in **1898 by William Claxton Peppe** at a site identified with ancient **Kapilavastu**; the reliquary inscription is in the **Brahmi** script — not Kharosthi.
- By early 2026, **58 countries** had eliminated **at least one Neglected Tropical Disease (NTD)**, according to the World Health Organization. (NTDs are a group of diseases, such as leprosy and kala-azar, common among poorer populations.)

**Trade and diplomacy.**
- The **India-UK CETA** — the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement — was a major bilateral trade milestone of 2025-26.
- **India took over the BRICS chairship on 1 January 2026** and hosts the **18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi**. (BRICS = Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa and newer members.)

**Don't confuse.** The Piprahwa inscription is in **Brahmi**, not Kharosthi — this exact word is the trap.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- The four labour codes came into force nationally on 21 November 2025.
- MSME enhanced investment/turnover limits took effect on 1 April 2025.
- Piprahwa relics were discovered in 1898 by W.C. Peppe near Kapilavastu; the inscription is in Brahmi script.
- By early 2026, 58 countries had eliminated at least one Neglected Tropical Disease (WHO).
- India-UK CETA was a landmark 2025-26 trade agreement.
- India took the BRICS chair on 1 January 2026 and hosts the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.

items.title: National current-affairs timeline — recent additions (Sep 2025 & Sep 2026)
items.body:
**In one line.** National developments added to fill the thin September 2025 and September 2026 windows.

**Why it is asked.** These were headline events (GST 2.0, the new Vice-President, the MiG-21 retirement) that make natural single-fact questions. Current affairs in this app are updated through **9 October 2026**.

| Date | What happened | Why it matters for the exam |
|---|---|---|
| 3 Sep 2025 | GST reforms ('GST 2.0') — rates cut and simplified on many goods | Tax-reform recall (GST = Goods and Services Tax) |
| 9/12 Sep 2025 | C. P. Radhakrishnan elected 15th Vice-President (early poll after Dhankhar resigned) | Current office-holder |
| 13 Sep 2025 | PM Modi's first Manipur visit since the May 2023 violence | Topical governance point |
| 15 Sep 2025 | Supreme Court stays parts of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 | Topical law point |
| 26 Sep 2025 | Indian Air Force formally retires the MiG-21 fleet after about 62 years | Defence milestone |
| 27 Sep 2025 | Cold Desert (Himachal Pradesh) designated a UNESCO biosphere reserve | Environment recall |
| 12-13 Sep 2026 | 18th BRICS Summit, New Delhi — New Delhi Declaration adopted | Summit host and outcome |

**Remember it:** 15th Vice-President = C. P. Radhakrishnan (oath 12 Sep 2025); the 18th BRICS Summit was in New Delhi (Sep 2026).

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- GST 2.0 reforms announced 3 Sep 2025 (rate rationalisation).
- C. P. Radhakrishnan — 15th Vice-President (oath 12 Sep 2025).
- SC stayed parts of Waqf (Amendment) Act 2025 on 15 Sep 2025.
- IAF retired MiG-21 on 26 Sep 2025 after ~62 years.
- 18th BRICS Summit held at New Delhi, 12-13 Sep 2026 (New Delhi Declaration).
